name: Eating disorder-adjacent restriction ('thinspo' leanness)
lead: Thinspiration ("thinspo") is imagery and content of thin people, associated with pro-ana (pro-anorexia) online communities that promote behaviours linked to anorexia nervosa.[1] In looksmaxxing contexts, extreme restriction to reach a lean or gaunt look is sometimes discussed, and medical groups regard restrictive eating of this kind as carrying eating disorder risk.[1]

Eating disorder organisations such as ANAD, NEDA and the Academy for Eating Disorders have criticised pro-ana sites for glamorising illness.[1] If you or someone you know is affected, local eating disorder helplines and healthcare providers offer support.

paras: Pro-ana sites first appeared in the late 1990s, and a second wave followed blogs and social networks in the 2000s.[1] Platforms including Yahoo, Tumblr, Pinterest and Instagram have introduced policies against such content, with limited effect.[1]

A 2006 Stanford study found that 35.5 percent of eating disorder patients had visited pro-ana sites, and 96 percent of those learned new weight-loss or purging methods there.[1] Some researchers argue the link between these sites and eating disorder rates is weak and that the sites mainly make affected people more visible.[1] Women who viewed the sites reported more negative mood and lower self-esteem in experimental studies.[1]
No studies found on restriction for looksmaxxing specifically. Studies of pro-ana site exposure are summarised above.[1]

timeline.event: Yahoo removes pro-ana groups from Yahoo Clubs.[1]
Tumblr, Pinterest and Instagram announce policies against pro-ana content.[1]

card.summary: Extreme restriction for a gaunt look, closely tied to eating disorder content.
card.note: Associated with documented eating disorder harms; seek professional support if affected.

quick.overview:
This entry covers restrictive eating aimed at extreme leanness, sharing ground with thinspiration and pro-ana content.

Medical organisations criticise such content, and research links exposure to worse mood and body image.
quick.mechanism: It involves severe caloric restriction and appearance-comparison content; no instructional detail is given here.
quick.risks: Anorexia nervosa is reported to have among the highest mortality of psychiatric disorders.[1] Support is available through eating disorder helplines and clinicians.
